name: Punk Protocol
one_liner: A front-running bot copied the Punk Protocol attacker's pool takeover and landed at index 50 vs his 52 in block 12995895 (43.33 vs 40.00 gwei): $5.95M USDT+DAI taken, $4.95M returned, $1M kept; it also mis-sent $3.0M USDC to the attacker. Pre-Merge, in-block evidence only.
delay_method: not measurable: no pre-inclusion mempool first-seen of the trigger tx
fate: 2021-08-10 19:20:03Z and 19:21:37Z (blocks 12999327, 12999334) the bot EOA sent 3,000,058.381173 USDT and 1,954,191.544043 DAI ($4,954,249.93) to Punk's deployer wallet, after Punk messaged the bot EOA at 12:03Z (it first thought the bot was the attacker) and the bot answered 'I frontran the real attacker' at 13:45Z. Before returning, at 19:17:54Z, the bot sold 1,000,000 DAI for 319.1843 ETH on 1inch: the $1M finder's fee Punk agreed ('after paying a fee of 1M DAI up to approximately 16% of the retrieved'). ETH figures here are stablecoin amounts divided by 3,119.7 USD/ETH (the attacker's 1inch rate). Share of the $8.95M drained: 55.4%; of the bot's own USDT+DAI take: 83.2%. The $2.996M USDC the bot mis-sent to the attacker was not recovered (sold for 960.3 ETH, 968 ETH to Tornado Cash); the attacker also took 45,100 DAI in a second tx and ignored Punk's on-chain message.
evidence_strength_basis: Call-tree diff of both traces, receipts' Transfer logs, anvil fork replay of both orders, trace_filter proof that only the deployer, the bot and the attacker ever called initialize() on the pools, the bot's own on-chain messages, return txs, and Punk's incident report (via Wayback) all saved under data/raw/ or incidents/punk-2021/. Unknown: when the bot first saw the attacker's pending tx (no mempool archive before 2023).
loot_note: Scope = the bot tx. gross_loot_eth covers everything it took from the pools ($8,950,039); 2,995,825 USDC of that was sent on to the attacker by the bot's copy error, so the bot's own side is $5,954,214 (bot_net_eth = that / 3,119.7 minus the tx's gas fee 0.03348 ETH, of which 0.01028 ETH tip to the miner and the rest burned as base fee). No coinbase payment. The attacker's tx in the same block paid a 0.00752 ETH tip and withdrew dust. Counterfactual (anvil): the attacker alone would have received $8,950,039.12.

name: Euler Finance: copied exploit contract executes the DAI-market exploit first, proceeds routed to the hacker by a hard-coded destination
one_liner: A fresh EOA copied the Euler attacker's exploit contract one block after its deploy, swapping only the owner address, and ran its DAI-market entry point at block 16817996 position 0: 8,877,507 DAI out of Euler. Funds went to the attacker's hard-coded wallet; the copier captured nothing.
delay_method: not measurable: no pre-inclusion mempool first-seen of the trigger tx
fate: Nothing reached Euler from this row. The copier's contract can only pay the address hard-coded in its bytecode, so its withdraw() (block 16818823, about 2 h 47 min after the exploit) sent all 8,877,507.35 DAI to the attacker's wallet. The copier's on-chain message (tx 0x44b559c8, block 16818973) says it tried to return the money and 'unfortunately it sent the money to the hacker's address'. Any later return by the Euler hacker to Euler is outside this row and not covered by our saved files.
evidence_strength_basis: The copier may be the attacker’s own second account: it was a fresh single-purpose EOA, kept the attacker’s cash-out wallet and captured nothing. Its own on-chain message is the only claim that it was a bot.
caveat: The copier may be the attacker’s own second account: it was a fresh single-purpose EOA, kept the attacker’s cash-out wallet and captured nothing. Its own on-chain message is the only claim that it was a bot.
loot_note: bot_net_eth is 0: the copier captured nothing. The DAI sat in its copy until the copier itself called withdraw() (tx 0xdae809e4, block 16818823), which sent all 8,877,507.35 DAI to the wallet baked into the creation code (0xb66cd966670d962c227b3eaba30a872dbfb995db, the attacker's wallet). Costs are NOT netted: the attack tx cost 0.1108 ETH of gas (0.0739 ETH tip + base fee), about 0.61 ETH across all the copier's txs per incident.json. Euler's net DAI-market loss in this tx was 8,904,507.35 DAI (Euler paid out 38,904,507.35 DAI and received 30,000,000 DAI); the whole Euler hack is about $197M (PeckShield figure, not re-verified here). No coinbase transfer: the tip (0.0739 ETH) is 78% of the 0.09425 ETH winning bid, so position 0 came from the public gas-price auction, not a bundle. No builder refund seen.
